create_campaign.title: Create campaign
create_campaign.description: Create a new LinkedIn outreach campaign in a workspace. Pick the channel with `type` and the writing mode with `mode`: AI mode writes a personalised message per prospect and needs writing_style_id and outreach_language; TEMPLATED mode sends one fixed template and needs template_id. Prospects are imported from input_url (a Sales Navigator search or a LinkedIn post). The campaign is created in TRAINING status; call start_campaign to begin outreach.

type.description: Channel: MESSAGING sends a connection request then messages, FIRST_DEGREE_MESSAGE messages existing connections, INMAIL sends InMails.

mode.description: AI writes a personalised message per prospect (needs writing_style_id and outreach_language); TEMPLATED sends the same fixed template to everyone (needs template_id).

workspace_id.description: Workspace id, from list_workspaces. User API keys can reach several workspaces; a workspace key is locked to its own.

workspace_product_id.description: Workspace product the outreach pitches, from list_workspace_products.

writing_style_id.description: Writing style for AI mode, from list_writing_styles. Required when mode is AI.

template_id.description: Message template for TEMPLATED mode, from list_templates. Its type must match the campaign type.

outreach_count_per_day.description: How many new prospects the campaign contacts per day (at least 1).

auto_pilot.description: true sends messages without manual approval; false queues every message for approval (see list_approval_messages).

outreach_language.description: Language outreach is written in, e.g. English or French.

included_profiles.description: Which profiles to include, e.g. ALL.

withdraw_request_after.description: Days after which an unanswered connection request is withdrawn.

is_blank_connect.description: true sends the connection request with no note.

follow_up_config.description: Follow-up schedule: keys f_1..f_10, each the number of days to wait before that follow-up, e.g. {"f_1": 3, "f_2": 7}.

re_engagement_config.description: Re-engagement schedule: keys r_1..r_12, each a wait in days that must be one of 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21.

prospect_enrichment_config.description: Up to 5 research agents to run before message generation (AI mode), e.g. prospect_deep_dive, company_deep_dive, recent_news, hiring_trends, fundraising_history, leadership_team, press_releases.

input_type.description: Where prospects come from: SALES_NAV_SEARCH_URL (a Sales Navigator or LinkedIn people-search URL) or LINKEDIN_POST_URL (people who engaged with a post). Pair with input_url.

input_url.description: The search or post URL matching input_type. Truncated URLs and lnkd.in short links are rejected.

scrape_reactions.description: For LINKEDIN_POST_URL: import people who reacted to the post.

scrape_comments.description: For LINKEDIN_POST_URL: import people who commented on the post.

output.description: The create campaign result: campaign.

campaign.description: Fields: id, name, status, type, created_at.

edit_message_draft.title: Edit message draft
edit_message_draft.description: Edit the body of an unsent message draft. Works for every draft in the sequence: the first outreach message, follow-ups, and re-engagements alike. A draft stays editable while it is pending approval and after it has been approved but not yet sent (the send path reads the latest body at send time), so an approved draft can still be corrected before its send window. Once a message has been sent it can no longer be edited. An already-sent message returns 400. A 409 is reserved for the narrow case where the message is sent concurrently, after this request read its status but before the write lands. A draft stays editable after its campaign is deleted, matching the in-app behaviour.

list_response_drafts.title: List response drafts
list_response_drafts.description: List AI-drafted responses to prospect replies (the "Response Ready" approvals). These are the replies Valley drafts once a prospect answers, and they are NOT returned by /public/v1/approvals/messages on any view, which covers first-touch and follow-up drafts only. Workspace admins and owners see every campaign in the workspace; members see only their own. Note that a pending draft is discarded server-side when the prospect sends a newer message, or when the account owner replies manually in LinkedIn, so an item can disappear between polls; approving an id that is already gone returns 404, and approving one that goes stale mid-request returns 409. Treat this as a live queue, not a ledger.

approve_and_send_response.title: Approve and send response
approve_and_send_response.description: Approve an AI-drafted response and send it to the prospect. Unlike outreach approval there is no scheduler in between: the reply goes out during this request and the draft moves straight to SENT. Pass an edited `message` to send different copy than the draft; the stored draft is updated to what was actually sent. A draft that was already sent returns 400. An id that no longer exists returns 404, which includes a draft the server discarded before this request arrived. A draft that was still pending when this request claimed it, but whose conversation moved on before it could send, is discarded here and returns 409, as does losing a race to another approval of the same draft.

message_id.description: Message id, from list_approval_messages (or list_response_drafts for reply drafts).

message.description: Optional edited body to send instead of the draft. Validated against the same per-type character limits as PATCH /approvals/messages/{id}.

output.description: The approve and send response result: messageId, messageType, campaignId, prospectId, conversationId, status.
